A variance ratio below one is consistent with reduced dispersion among the detector-paired values, but it does not identify the cause. Reconstruction smoothing, detector selection, unequal beat counts, order-based mispairing, or record exclusions can all contribute. A ratio above one is equally important counterevidence to any universal shrinkage narrative. At this partial stage the correct use is failure-mode discovery and evaluator validation, not selection of a winning loss mask.
The currently accepted generation is the only basis for these plots. Earlier order-truncated artifacts remain visible in the exclusion ledger but are not carried forward as evidence. During a code-generation transition, zero accepted rows is therefore the correct fail-closed result rather than an invitation to reuse otherwise plausible historical values.

The first controlled accepted family is now complete: 1000000–1000004, all at seed 42 with identical binary factors. The levels are none, global adaptive RBF, anatomical Laplacian, anatomical multiscale IMQ, and temporal K-means multiscale IMQ. Direction counts are deliberately not collapsed into a score. Relative to level 0, levels 1–4 lower absolute aggregate bias in 6/12, 9/12, 8/12, and 8/12 rows; move variance closer to one in 9/12, 10/12, 10/12, and 11/12; lower feature-wise distribution MMD² in 7/12, 10/12, 10/12, and 9/12; and improve full-denominator pair coverage in 8/12, 3/12, 7/12, and 8/12 rows. No kernel dominates all four axes.
The patient-level contrasts make the trade-offs more concrete. Anatomical Laplacian produces the largest V6-QT common-pair MAE decrease, about 20.3 ms, but loses 6.64 percentage points of full-denominator pair coverage. Global RBF lowers the same MAE by about 15.8 ms while increasing coverage by 1.23 points, even though its aggregate mean QT bias changes sign and grows in absolute value. Anatomical multiscale IMQ lowers V6-QT MAE by 8.2 ms with a 0.41-point coverage loss, while temporal K-means multiscale IMQ lowers it by 14.3 ms with a 1.36-point loss. These common-pair MAE changes coexist with slightly worse final validation MSE for all four candidates. Aggregate bias, record-level MAE, distribution discrepancy, detector availability, and validation MSE therefore answer different questions; none can serve as a single winner metric.
These intervals are unadjusted, detector-conditioned, and limited to one seed and the records where both models yield finite pairs. They are useful for debugging the measurement contract and exposing endpoint discordance, not for declaring a kernel effect. Confirmatory inference still requires all seed blocks, prespecified contrasts, multiplicity control, and explicit handling of differential detector failure.
The current matcher resolves one major ambiguity but not every measurement problem. The full-denominator ledger, detector-state strata, patient-cluster summaries, and five-window sensitivity grid now expose several ways the 100 ms result can change. They do not prove that any window is clinically correct: the detector can move or omit fiducials systematically, no clinician-adjudicated fiducial subset is available, and the compact ledger cannot retrospectively evaluate an arbitrary unprespecified window. Confirmatory QT/amplitude conclusions still require completion across masks and seeds, multiplicity-aware patient-cluster inference, and detector validation against independently adjudicated fiducials.

17.9 Diagnostics still missing
Latent embeddings, kernel Gram matrices, gradient conflicts, Hessian spectra, noise response surfaces, calibration curves, and inference latency are worthwhile only when generated from named checkpoints and named records. Each future diagnostic must include its cohort, sampling rule, checkpoint digest, evaluation-code digest, random seed where applicable, and uncertainty. Until those artifacts exist, the book records the protocol rather than drawing decorative synthetic plots.

title: 18  Clinical Trust, Cath-Lab Safety, and Validation Requirements
text:
18.1 Current clinical-use boundary
Reconstructing a 12-lead ECG from three observed leads is an inverse problem, not a substitute for measuring all 12 leads. This chapter defines the evidence required before reconstructed signals can support ischemia, electrophysiology, or cath-lab claims. No STEMI AUROC, culprit-artery accuracy, mortality benefit, clinician confidence score, or workflow saving has been measured in this project; the previous synthetic examples have been withdrawn.
The models are research systems. Reconstructed leads must not trigger or cancel cath-lab activation, change medication, adjudicate QT safety, or replace a diagnostic 12-lead ECG. EchoNext and ECGFounder outputs are frozen-model transfer probes, not clinical adjudication.

18.2 Why global reconstruction accuracy is insufficient
Low MSE can coexist with attenuation of rare but decisive morphology. Cath-lab decisions depend on localized amplitude, timing, contiguity, reciprocal changes, and clinical context. A valid assessment therefore needs at least four linked levels:








Level
Unit
Required evidence




Signal
patient × lead × time
paired error, correlation, spectral distortion, uncertainty


Morphology
beat/segment
J point, ST deviation/slope, QRS, QT/QTc, T-wave and Q-wave measurements


Diagnostic
patient/encounter
blinded reference labels, sensitivity, specificity, calibration, decision curves


Workflow
site/clinician
prospective timing, overrides, failure modes, and patient-centered outcomes



Success at one level does not imply success at the next.

title: 18  Clinical Trust, Cath-Lab Safety, and Validation Requirements
text:
18.3 Prespecified ischemia validation
The ischemia cohort must be independent of training and contain acquisition-time 12-lead signals with expert adjudication. Evaluation should retain clinically relevant strata: anterior, inferior, lateral, posterior, right-ventricular, left-main-equivalent, paced rhythm, bundle-branch block, LVH, and non-ischemic ST–T abnormalities.
For each lead, measure signed and absolute J-point error at a prespecified offset, ST-slope error, T-wave polarity agreement, pathologic-Q agreement, and contiguous-lead pattern agreement. Patient-level diagnostic evaluation must report sensitivity at a prespecified false-positive rate, specificity, predictive values across plausible prevalence, calibration, and abstention coverage. Confidence intervals must be clustered by patient and site.

18.3.1 Non-inferiority is not “no significant difference”
For paired diagnostic performance D, the hypothesis must specify a clinically justified margin \delta before seeing test results:
H_0: D_{\mathrm{reconstructed}}-D_{\mathrm{measured}}\le -\delta.
Rejecting this null requires the lower confidence bound to exceed -\delta. Failure to detect a difference is not evidence of non-inferiority.

18.5 Culprit-artery localization requires a different reference standard
LAD/RCA/LCx localization cannot be inferred responsibly from reconstruction metrics. It requires angiographic or adjudicated procedural ground truth, explicit handling of multivessel disease and prior infarction, temporal alignment between ECG and angiography, and a protocol for indeterminate cases. Any localization classifier must be frozen before external testing and compared against measured-ECG performance on the same encounters.

title: 18  Clinical Trust, Cath-Lab Safety, and Validation Requirements
section: 18.6 EchoNext and ECGFounder: what they can and cannot show
text:
18.6 EchoNext and ECGFounder: what they can and cannot show
A frozen downstream classifier can test whether its outputs change when measured ECGs are replaced by reconstructions. Useful paired quantities include logit shift, rank correlation, task-wise AUROC difference, calibration change, and decision-threshold reclassification. These are model-mediated endpoints. They show compatibility with that frozen network, not preservation of every diagnosis and not agreement with clinicians.
The evaluation must disclose the classifier version, input scaling and lead order, label definitions, cohort overlap, missing-label handling, threshold selection, and confidence-interval method. Macro-averages must not hide task-level failures, especially for rare structural or conduction conditions.
crumbs: 18  Clinical Trust, Cath-Lab Safety, and Validation Requirements

title: 18  Clinical Trust, Cath-Lab Safety, and Validation Requirements
text:
18.7 Decision-curve and utility analysis
Decision curves are admissible only after calibrated patient-level probabilities exist. For threshold probability p_t, net benefit is
\mathrm{NB}(p_t)=\frac{\mathrm{TP}}{N}-\frac{\mathrm{FP}}{N}\frac{p_t}{1-p_t}.
The threshold encodes relative harm and cannot be chosen from the same test set to maximize apparent benefit. Mortality, door-to-balloon time, and cost effects require observed or externally justified inputs with sensitivity analysis; they must never be invented from reconstruction accuracy.
crumbs: 18  Clinical Trust, Cath-Lab Safety, and Validation Requirements

title: 18  Clinical Trust, Cath-Lab Safety, and Validation Requirements
text:
18.8 Human-factors study before workflow claims
A blinded, randomized reader study should compare measured ECG, reduced-lead ECG, and reduced-lead-plus-reconstruction conditions. It needs prespecified readers, washout, case-order randomization, time measurement, confidence capture, override/abstention options, and multi-reader multi-case analysis. The primary question is whether reconstruction changes correct decisions without increasing unsafe false reassurance.

title: Benchmarking Loss Functions for Electrocardiogram Reconstruction
text: Preface & Executive Summary

title: Benchmarking Loss Functions for Electrocardiogram Reconstruction
text:
Motivation & Clinical Context
Electrocardiogram (ECG) reconstruction aims to estimate a complete 12-lead ECG representation from a reduced subset of leads—such as a single wearable-like Lead I or a 3-lead input. Mean Squared Error (MSE) is a standard objective, but conditional averaging can attenuate morphology when the missing signal is not uniquely determined by the observed leads. This handbook tests that concern rather than assuming it.

The Regression-to-the-Mean Failure (Presacan et al., 2025)
In Communications Medicine (Nature Portfolio), Presacan et al. (2025) reported regression-to-the-mean behavior in ECG reconstruction trained with MSE. More generally, squared-error population risk targets a conditional expectation; when multiple missing-lead morphologies are compatible with the observed leads, averaging can attenuate uncommon amplitudes or shapes. Whether that occurs for a particular checkpoint and endpoint is measured here rather than assumed from the theorem or prior paper.
Potential failure modes include P/T delineation error, ST-segment attenuation, and QT/QTc drift. These are hypotheses requiring artifact-backed evaluation; the book does not infer patient harm from synthetic waveforms or global similarity metrics.
       MSE Loss (Regression to Mean)          Combinatorial Composite Loss (Ours)
    ┌─────────────────────────────────┐      ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Flat P-waves / Flattened ST    │      │  Candidate shape preservation  │
    │  Damped Peak Amplitudes         │  vs  │  QTc/VCG metrics require audit │
    │  Metrics requiring audit        │      │  No assumed clinical benefit   │
    └─────────────────────────────────┘      └─────────────────────────────────┘

title: Benchmarking Loss Functions for Electrocardiogram Reconstruction
text:
How to read this handbook
For current experiment status, start with the Live Experiment Observatory, then open either the three-lead ECG-AIM analysis or the one-lead wavelet/SSL analysis. Those pages query the live databases on every render and keep the two experimental contracts separate.
The book begins with evidence, not demonstrations. The opening real-data EDA audits PTB-XL and EchoNext in depth and now provides separate, stability-audited waveform UMAPs for every locally supported clinical cohort: PTB-XL, EchoNext, LUDB, ISP, Sunnybrook, Zhejiang, and RDB. The multi-dataset atlas establishes what the smaller morphology cohorts contribute, followed by a separate Zhejiang file-level audit. Only after those measurement contracts are visible does the PTB-XL preprocessing contract explain the content-pinned tensors and lead mapping.
The remaining parts follow the causal order of the study:

Data, cohorts, and measurement — what was observed, how records were partitioned, and which claims each dataset can support.
Reconstruction models and objectives — the architectures and loss terms applied to those inputs.
Clinical and statistical evaluation — paired morphology, delineation, agreement, fairness, robustness, and uncertainty.
Benchmark and external validation — the locked 48-cell evidence, the still-training mixed-level factorial study, device transfer, and EchoNext classifier preservation.

This order is deliberate. A model ranking is uninterpretable until the reader knows the units, split boundary, repeated-patient structure, endpoint prevalence, and downstream measurement contract. Synthetic examples remain in the book as executable tutorials, but they are labeled as demonstrations and never substitute for cohort evidence.

Open this rendered index.html, then use the persistent sidebar or the Previous/Next controls. The five parts and all chapters are members of one Quarto book; tables, figures, equation numbers, citations, and section references share one navigation structure.

title: 3  One-Lead Wavelet and SSL: Live Results
text:
3.2 Registered comparison hierarchy
The principal comparison is:
A0 → A0 + wavelet → A0 + wavelet + SSL.
E1 is reserved for complementarity:
A0 + wavelet + SSL versus E1 + wavelet + SSL.
Current 1110000 evidence does not authorize calling E1 an improved base architecture. The highest-value mechanism contrast is matched Morlet magnitude + Morlet phase versus Morlet magnitude + UEG-repolarization phase. A replicated gain concentrated on T-on/T-off would be consistent with the physiological second-view hypothesis, but detector artifacts, leakage, and generic regularization remain alternative explanations requiring controls.

            base[f"improvement.{metric}"]=sign*(row[metric+"_right"]-row[metric+"_left"])
        contrast_rows.append(base)
contrast_table=pd.DataFrame(contrast_rows)
display(contrast_table if not contrast_table.empty else pd.DataFrame([{"status":"no registered contrast currently estimable"}]))

title: 4  Real-Cohort EDA, Integrity Checks, and Deep Diagnostics
text:
4.1 Evidence map
This is the first numbered chapter because every later result inherits its data contract. It replaces “representative synthetic ECG” reasoning with an auditable description of the data actually present in this repository. The analysis has three levels: metadata integrity, signal integrity, and task integrity. A reconstruction benchmark is only interpretable when all three hold.
Every executable audit below resolves its input beneath ../data/ and prints the resolved path. No waveform statistic in this chapter is generated from the later synthetic tutorials.
These artifacts do not support the same inference. PTB-XL is the reconstruction development cohort. EchoNext is an external transfer cohort with echocardiography-derived labels. Performance on EchoNext tests transport under a different sampling and normalization pipeline; it does not retroactively enlarge the PTB-XL training set.

section: 4.2 PTB-XL: observed cohort and split contract
text:
4.2 PTB-XL: observed cohort and split contract
The local metadata contain 21,799 ECG records and 28 columns. The ten official stratification folds are nearly balanced (2,173–2,198 records each). The locked model registry maps folds 1–8 to training (17,418 records), fold 9 to validation (2,183), and fold 10 to test (2,198). The registry also reports 1,904 unique patients in the test set, so patient-clustered uncertainty is necessary: record-level resampling would treat repeated ECGs from the same person as independent.
The raw age field deserves an explicit validity audit. Its observed maximum is 300, which is not physiologically plausible as years and should not silently enter subgroup analysis. Age-based EDA must therefore report invalid-value counts and either use a documented correction supplied by the dataset or mark those values missing. It must not “fix” them by clipping without a sensitivity analysis.


Code
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

ROOT = Path("..")
ptb = pd.read_csv(ROOT / "data/ptb_xl/ptbxl_database.csv")

ptb_audit = pd.DataFrame({
    "quantity": [
        "records", "unique patients", "male-coded (sex=0)",
        "female-coded (sex=1)", "age missing", "age outside [0,120]",
        "fold-10 test records", "fold-10 unique patients"
    ],
    "value": [
        len(ptb), ptb.patient_id.nunique(), (ptb.sex == 0).sum(),
        (ptb.sex == 1).sum(), ptb.age.isna().sum(),
        (~ptb.age.between(0, 120)).sum(), (ptb.strat_fold == 10).sum(),
        ptb.loc[ptb.strat_fold == 10, "patient_id"].nunique()
    ]
})

4.2.1 Leakage checks that must precede modeling

Patient separation: intersect patient IDs across train, validation, and test. Every intersection must be empty.
File inventory: confirm every metadata row resolves to exactly one waveform tensor in its assigned split.
Duplicate signals: hash waveform bytes after canonical dtype conversion. Metadata uniqueness alone cannot detect copied signals.
Label derivation: parse scp_codes deterministically and version the superclass mapping.
Preprocessing fit scope: any learned mean, variance, clipping threshold, or calibration parameter must be fit on training data only.

4.2.2 PTB-XL demographic and diagnostic composition
The next audit separates record counts from patient counts, treats ages outside 0–120 as missing, and derives diagnostic superclasses from the local scp_statements.csv mapping. Superclass counts are multilabel record counts, so their sum can exceed the number of ECGs.


Code
import ast

ptb["analysis_split"] = np.select(
    [ptb.strat_fold <= 8, ptb.strat_fold == 9, ptb.strat_fold == 10],
    ["train", "validation", "test"],
    default="unassigned",
)
ptb["age_valid"] = ptb.age.where(ptb.age.between(0, 120))
ptb_demographics = ptb.groupby("analysis_split").agg(
    records=("ecg_id", "size"),
    patients=("patient_id", "nunique"),

4.2.3 Executed PTB-XL waveform audit
The following block reads the actual paired WFDB records named by filename_hr and filename_lr in data/ptb_xl/ptbxl_database.csv. To keep HTML rendering reproducible and bounded, it uses a fixed, fold-stratified audit sample of 25 records from each official fold (250 records total); this is an EDA sample, not an inferential subsample. Primary signal summaries use the stored 500 Hz physical waveforms. The paired 100 Hz releases are upsampled to quantify what a 100→500 Hz adapter can and cannot recover.


Code
import wfdb
from scipy.signal import resample_poly, welch

PTB_ROOT = (ROOT / "data/ptb_xl").resolve()
audit_rows = (
    ptb.groupby("strat_fold", group_keys=False)
       .sample(n=25, random_state=20260731)
       .sort_values(["strat_fold", "ecg_id"])
)
signals_hr = []
signals_lr_up = []
for row in audit_rows[["filename_hr", "filename_lr"]].itertuples(index=False):
    signal_hr, fields_hr = wfdb.rdsamp(str(PTB_ROOT / row.filename_hr))
    signal_lr, fields_lr = wfdb.rdsamp(str(PTB_ROOT / row.filename_lr))
    if fields_hr["fs"] != 500 or signal_hr.shape != (5000, 12):
        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected PTB-XL high-resolution contract: {row.filename_hr}")
    if fields_lr["fs"] != 100 or signal_lr.shape != (1000, 12):
        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected PTB-XL low-resolution contract: {row.filename_lr}")
    if fields_hr["sig_name"] != fields_lr["sig_name"]:
        raise ValueError(f"Lead-order mismatch: {row.filename_hr} vs {row.filename_lr}")
    signals_hr.append(signal_hr.astype(np.float32))
    signals_lr_up.append(
        resample_poly(signal_lr, up=5, down=1, axis=0).astype(np.float32)
    )
ptb_wave = np.stack(signals_hr)  # records × 5000 samples × leads
ptb_lr_up = np.stack(signals_lr_up)
fields = fields_hr
lead_names = fields["sig_name"]

finite = np.isfinite(ptb_wave)
lead_sd = ptb_wave.std(axis=1)
freq, psd = welch(ptb_wave, fs=500, axis=1, nperseg=1024)
band_power = {
    "baseline_<0.5Hz": np.trapz(psd[:, (freq < 0.5), :], freq[freq < 0.5], axis=1),
    "cardiac_0.5-40Hz": np.trapz(
        psd[:, (freq >= 0.5) & (freq <= 40), :],
        freq[(freq >= 0.5) & (freq <= 40)], axis=1
    ),
    "high_40-150Hz": np.trapz(
        psd[:, (freq > 40) & (freq <= 150), :],
        freq[(freq > 40) & (freq <= 150)], axis=1
    ),
}

ptb_signal_audit = pd.DataFrame({
    "lead": lead_names,
    "finite_percent": 100 * finite.mean(axis=(0, 1)),
    "p01_mV": np.quantile(ptb_wave, 0.01, axis=(0, 1)),
    "median_mV": np.median(ptb_wave, axis=(0, 1)),
    "p99_mV": np.quantile(ptb_wave, 0.99, axis=(0, 1)),
    "median_RMS_mV": np.median(np.sqrt(np.mean(ptb_wave ** 2, axis=1)), axis=0),
    "near_flat_records_percent": 100 * (lead_sd < 1e-4).mean(axis=0),
    "median_high_frequency_fraction": np.median(
        band_power["high_40-150Hz"] /
        np.maximum(
            band_power["cardiac_0.5-40Hz"] + band_power["high_40-150Hz"],
            1e-12
        ),
        axis=0
    ),
})
print(f"Loaded {len(ptb_wave)} paired 500 Hz/100 Hz real records from {PTB_ROOT}")

Because 100 Hz data have a 50 Hz Nyquist limit, upsampling cannot restore true 40–150 Hz content present in the 500 Hz release. The paired error above measures the complete adapter discrepancy; final morphology analysis should additionally compare QRS-band power and fiducials before and after any model-specific resampling.


4.2.4 The actual model-input tensor boundary
Raw WFDB EDA is necessary but not sufficient: the reconstruction code does not read WFDB files during training. scripts/train_mcma_3lead.py::PTBXLDataset loads .pt files, expects shape 12 × 5000, appends 120 zeros to reach a pooling-compatible length of 5,120, and selects lead indices [0, 1, 7]—I, II, and V2—as the model input. Targets contain all 12 padded leads. The training loader applies no per-record standardization, filtering, or amplitude clipping.
The following audit is computed over every tensor, not the 250-record raw-waveform sample. To keep routine book renders tractable, scripts/audit_ptbxl_tensors_for_book.py performs the 5 GB sequential scan with the project venv and writes a record-level Parquet plus a JSON summary. Each tensor is loaded through torch.load(..., weights_only=True) and checked for metadata/split alignment, shape, dtype, nonfinite values, flat leads, amplitude, RMS, and SHA-256 of canonical float32 signal bytes.

The executed gate finds all 21,799 of 21,799 expected tensors in the correct split, all with shape 12 × 5000, dtype float32, finite values, and unique canonical signal hashes. It also finds one concrete quality exception: training ECG 12722 has an exactly zero V5 lead. That record should be retained in the cohort ledger and handled by an explicit quality policy, not silently disappear inside a data loader.
The gate distinguishes three failure classes. A missing tensor is a cohort-definition error; a malformed/nonfinite tensor is a preprocessing error; a duplicate canonical hash is a potential leakage or export error requiring record-level adjudication. A perfectly matched inventory does not by itself prove the correct physical units, so the next two checks inspect the distribution and pair tensors back to the raw 500 Hz waveforms.

text:
4.3 EchoNext: population, waveform, and endpoint audit
The local EchoNext metadata table contains 100,000 records and 39 fields. The frozen external test array contains 5,442 × 1 × 2,500 × 12 values. At the declared 250 Hz, each trace spans 10 seconds. The singleton axis is a storage/channel wrapper, not an ECG lead. Lead order is explicitly:
[I,II,III,aVR,aVL,aVF,V_1,V_2,V_3,V_4,V_5,V_6].
The waveforms are stored as float64 after official per-lead clipping and train-set z-scoring. Evaluation inverts that affine transform back to clipped microvolts before reconstruction inference. This is a critical domain-transfer detail because PTB-XL models expect 500 Hz, 5,000-sample, physical-mV inputs with no per-record normalization. Resampling, unit conversion, axis ordering, and inverse normalization must all be validated independently.
Only the EchoNext test waveform array is present under the local data/echonext/ tree. Train, validation, and no_split waveform distributions therefore cannot be compared from this repository snapshot; their metadata are auditable, but claiming split-wise waveform parity would exceed the available artifact.
The 100,000-row metadata split is 72,475 train, 4,626 validation, 5,442 test, and 17,457 marked no_split. The unsplit records must not be silently added to training: their role is undefined by the local split field. The cohort is 53,581 male and 46,419 female records, with age 18–90 years (median 63; mean 61.18). Acquisition settings are heavily clinical—48,162 inpatient and 31,453 emergency records, compared with 17,194 outpatient and 3,191 procedural records—so this is not a consumer-wearable population sample.
Race/ethnicity counts are 31,013 Hispanic, 29,211 White, 16,461 Black, 3,428 Asian, 7,429 other, and 12,458 unknown. These are record counts rather than unique-patient counts and should not be presented as independent population denominators when patients have repeated ECGs.

text:
4.4 Endpoint prevalence and effective difficulty
The EchoNext classifier evaluates 12 echo-derived structural-heart-disease endpoints on the same 5,442 test records. Prevalence ranges from 0.37% (20 pulmonary-regurgitation positives) to 42.59% (2,318 composite SHD positives). Consequently:

accuracy is misleading for rare endpoints;
AUROC can look respectable while precision remains low;
average precision must be interpreted against prevalence;
F1 at a fixed 0.5 threshold mixes discrimination with calibration and threshold transport;
confidence intervals for the rarest endpoints will be wide even with 5,442 records.

title: 4  Real-Cohort EDA, Integrity Checks, and Deep Diagnostics
text:
4.6 Signal-level EDA: what to measure

4.6.1 1. Units and inverse normalization
For each lead \ell, recover clipped microvolts using
x_{\mu V,\ell}=z_\ell\sigma_\ell+\mu_\ell.
Then convert once to millivolts if the reconstruction model expects mV:
x_{mV,\ell}=10^{-3}x_{\mu V,\ell}.
A thousand-fold unit error can produce finite tensors and plausible-looking normalized plots while destroying inference. Unit tests should assert known percentile ranges before and after conversion.


4.6.2 2. Clipping occupancy
Compute the fraction of values equal, or numerically close, to each provenance bound by lead. High occupancy indicates censored amplitude tails. Report this because peak-amplitude and ST-deviation errors are then conditional on the released clipping policy.
The rendered audit below reads a deterministic 256-record sample from the memory-mapped array, reverses the released affine normalization using PROVENANCE.json, and recomputes signal-validity and lead-law summaries. The compact disk does not retain a hash-bound full-array clipping audit, so this chapter does not present hard-coded full-array percentiles or occupancies as current evidence.


Code
rng = np.random.default_rng(20260731)
echo_idx = np.sort(rng.choice(wave.shape[0], size=256, replace=False))
z = np.asarray(wave[echo_idx, 0, :, :], dtype=np.float64)
means = np.asarray(provenance["normalization"]["mean"], dtype=float)
stds = np.asarray(provenance["normalization"]["std"], dtype=float)
echo_uv = z * stds + means

echo_laws = {
    "III-(II-I)": echo_uv[:, :, 2] - (echo_uv[:, :, 1] - echo_uv[:, :, 0]),
    "aVR+(I+II)/2": echo_uv[:, :, 3] + (echo_uv[:, :, 0] + echo_uv[:, :, 1]) / 2,
    "aVL-(I-II/2)": echo_uv[:, :, 4] - (echo_uv[:, :, 0] - echo_uv[:, :, 1] / 2),
    "aVF-(II-I/2)": echo_uv[:, :, 5] - (echo_uv[:, :, 1] - echo_uv[:, :, 0] / 2),
}
echo_live_audit = pd.DataFrame({
    "quantity": [
        "resolved waveform path", "sampled records", "finite values (%)",
        "global 0.1st percentile (µV)", "global 99.9th percentile (µV)",
        *[f"median record RMSE {name} (µV)" for name in echo_laws],
    ],
    "value": [
        str((ROOT / "data/echonext/EchoNext_test_waveforms.npy").resolve()),
        len(echo_idx), 100 * np.isfinite(echo_uv).mean(),
        np.quantile(echo_uv, 0.001), np.quantile(echo_uv, 0.999),
        *[np.median(np.sqrt(np.mean(residual ** 2, axis=1)))
          for residual in echo_laws.values()],

})

Full-array clipping occupancy is a required future retained artifact. It must be computed in chunks, bound to the waveform/provenance hashes, and loaded here rather than transcribed into prose.


4.6.3 3. Lead-law residuals
The limb leads obey approximate linear relations:
III \approx II-I,\quad aVR \approx-\frac{I+II}{2},\quad
aVL \approx I-\frac{II}{2},\quad aVF \approx II-\frac{I}{2}.
Residual distributions detect lead permutations, polarity errors, scaling inconsistencies, and corrupted records. These are pipeline diagnostics, not targets to “repair” after looking at test performance.
The executable sample above supplies a regression diagnostic for the current local tensor. Full-array median and tail tolerances remain unreported until a hash-bound audit artifact is retained; sample estimates must not be promoted to full-cohort thresholds.


4.6.4 4. Spectral and morphology distributions
Report per-lead power in prespecified bands (baseline, P/T, QRS, high-frequency), R-peak count, RR variability, QRS width, QT/QTc, peak amplitude, and flatline fraction. Compare distributions before and after resampling. A global Pearson score can conceal loss of high-frequency QRS energy or systematic ST smoothing.


4.6.5 5. Cross-lead dependence
Plot the 12\times12 lead correlation matrix and the distribution of record-level condition numbers. Reconstruction difficulty depends on how much missing-lead information is identifiable from observed leads I, II, and V_2 (indices 0, 1, 7 in the locked registry). Strong average correlation does not imply that diagnostically important residual variation is recoverable.

title: 4  Real-Cohort EDA, Integrity Checks, and Deep Diagnostics
text:
4.7 Deep reconstruction diagnostics
A useful diagnostic stack separates four questions.








Layer
Question
Minimum outputs




Sample fidelity
Are point amplitudes close?
MAE/MSE, bias, Bland–Altman, peak error


Shape fidelity
Are morphology and timing preserved?
Pearson, derivative error, DTW, delineation deltas


Physiologic consistency
Do leads form a coherent ECG?
Einthoven residuals, VCG trajectory error, interval consistency


Diagnostic utility
Does a frozen model retain predictions?
per-task AUROC/AP/F1, calibration, paired probability drift



Failure analysis should be record based, not figure based. Rank records separately by MSE, missing-lead Pearson, QRS error, ST error, classifier probability drift, and signal-quality score. The intersection and disagreement among those lists reveal different failure modes:

low MSE + poor classifier fidelity: small but task-aligned feature loss;
high MSE + stable classifier output: nuisance amplitude or baseline mismatch;
strong global Pearson + poor QRS correlation: localized depolarization failure;
good morphology + lead-law violation: cross-lead incoherence;
good mean performance + subgroup tail failure: deployment inequity.

title: 4  Real-Cohort EDA, Integrity Checks, and Deep Diagnostics
section: 4.8 Statistical design for the factorial benchmark
text:
4.8 Statistical design for the factorial benchmark
The registered experiment is a 3\times2^4 grid, but primary factorial inference is the MSE-on 3\times2^3 subset. Eight MultiScale-VAE MSE-toggle cells are quarantined because paired checkpoints were tensor-identical under a historical decoder-loss defect. The complete 48-row table is useful for identity and forensics; it is not a uniformly valid four-factor inferential grid.
Use paired patient-cluster BCa intervals because all cells predict the same test patients and some patients contribute multiple records. For each family and endpoint, estimate
\Delta_k=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid k=1]-\mathbb{E}[Y\mid k=0]
and prespecified two-way interactions. Family-wise morphology tests use the repository’s corrected threshold; exploratory downstream endpoints must be labeled exploratory. The existing results show significant QRS and ST improvements for full-versus-base in all three architecture families, while ECGFounder AUROC changes are not significant. That supports improved morphology without detected diagnostic-utility loss; it is not proof of clinical equivalence.

title: 4  Real-Cohort EDA, Integrity Checks, and Deep Diagnostics
text:
4.9 Reproducible audit checklist

Record exact file hashes and waveform shapes.
Assert patient-disjoint splits and stable record order.
Validate axis order, lead order, sampling rate, unit, and duration.
Quantify invalid demographics and structured missingness.
Report endpoint support before any classifier metric.
Preserve rare-task uncertainty; do not hide it in macro averages.
Compare pre/post-resampling spectra and intervals.
Inspect clipping occupancy and lead-law residuals.
Use patient-clustered paired inference.
Publish per-record outputs so tail failures remain inspectable.

title: 5  Dataset Atlas: LUDB, ISP, and Sunnybrook
text:
5.1 Provenance and governance ledger
LUDB, ISP, and Sunnybrook are complementary, not interchangeable. LUDB supplies dense lead-specific morphology annotations; ISP supplies interval targets for delineation; Sunnybrook supplies a small external set of fully measured clinical ECGs. A pooled “multi-dataset score” would erase those distinctions.
The local files do not all have the same documentation status. LUDB is the public PhysioNet release v1.0.1, cited as Kalyakulina et al. with DOI 10.13026/eegm-h675, and is distributed under the Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0. Its source states that 200 ten-second ECGs were collected in 2017–2018, annotated by cardiologists, with written consent and institutional review approval. EchoNext is a restricted PhysioNet resource; local provenance pins IntroECG commit 15233e… but does not attest which PhysioNet release version it corresponds to. The canonical dataset record and version history are available under DOI 10.13026/2j37-ba56.
The ISP folder in this repository does not include a citation, version, license, data-use terms, or a source identifier. Its three class meanings and sampling rate therefore remain unknown in this book. Sunnybrook has a local METADATA.json and README but no accompanying license, cohort selection protocol, subject identifiers, consent/ethics statement, or distribution authority. Until those fields are supplied by the data owner, Sunnybrook is a local exploratory transfer set and ISP is a locally present delineation artifact—not a fully provenance-resolved public benchmark.

5.1.1 Reproducible local fingerprints
The following fingerprints identify the exact artifacts read by this book. A tree hash includes each relative path, file size, and file digest, so a renamed, added, removed, or changed record alters the result.


Code
def file_sha256(path, chunk_size=8 * 1024 * 1024):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(chunk_size), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()

def tree_sha256(root, patterns):
    files = sorted({
        path for pattern in patterns for path in root.rglob(pattern)
        if path.is_file()
    })
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    total_bytes = 0
    for path in files:
        size = path.stat().st_size
        total_bytes += size
        digest.update(str(path.relative_to(root)).encode())
        digest.update(str(size).encode())
        digest.update(file_sha256(path).encode())
    return len(files), total_bytes, digest.hexdigest()

fingerprints = []
for dataset, root, patterns in [
    ("LUDB", ROOT / "data/ludb", ["*.hea", "*.dat", "*.atr_*", "README", "LICENSE.txt"]),
    ("ISP", ROOT / "data/isp_delineation_dataset", ["*.hea", "*.dat", "*.csv"]),
    ("Sunnybrook", ROOT / "data/sunnybrook_12_lead_ecg_samples", ["*.xml", "*.csv", "*.json", "*.md"]),
]:
    n_files, n_bytes, digest = tree_sha256(root, patterns)
    fingerprints.append({
        "dataset": dataset, "resolved_root": str(root.resolve()),
        "files_hashed": n_files, "bytes_hashed": n_bytes, "sha256_tree": digest,
    })

for name in [
    "echonext_metadata_100k.csv", "EchoNext_test_waveforms.npy", "PROVENANCE.json"
]:
    path = ROOT / "data/echonext" / name

All 200 records should share exactly one schema. A mismatch is an integrity failure, not a reason to silently resample or reorder one record.


5.2.2 Demographics and diagnoses
The local headers yield 115 male and 85 female records. Age ranges from 11 to 90 years (mean 51.98, median 56). Diagnoses are overlapping free-text statements. Frequent statements include sinus rhythm (143), left ventricular hypertrophy (108), left atrial hypertrophy (102), normal electrical axis (75), left-axis deviation (66), incomplete right bundle-branch block (29), sinus bradycardia (25), and atrial fibrillation (15).


Code
def parse_ludb_header(path):
    text = path.read_text()
    age = re.search(r"#<age>:\s*(\d+)", text)
    sex = re.search(r"#<sex>:\s*([MF])", text)
    statements = [
        line[1:].strip() for line in text.splitlines()
        if line.startswith("#") and not line.startswith("#<") and line[1:].strip()
    ]
    return {
        "age": int(age.group(1)) if age else np.nan,
        "sex": sex.group(1) if sex else "unknown",
        "statements": statements,
    }

ludb_meta = pd.DataFrame([
    {"record": rid, **parse_ludb_header(ludb_root / f"{rid}.hea")}
    for rid in record_ids

5.2.5 Diagnostics LUDB enables
For P, QRS, and T waves, report onset, peak, and offset error by lead. Matching must be beat-aware and limited to a physiologic window; unconstrained nearest-neighbor matching can pair adjacent cycles. Minimum outputs are sensitivity, positive predictive value, median/IQR/95th-percentile timing error, cycle-mismatch rate, error versus wave amplitude, and interval consistency across leads.
A reconstruction can have high sample correlation but erase a low-amplitude P wave or shift its boundary enough to corrupt PR measurement. LUDB is designed to reveal precisely that failure.

5.3 ISP delineation targets

5.3.1 Local data contract
The ISP CSVs contain 403 training and 72 test rows. Each row includes file_name, age, binary sex coding, and a serialized list of (class, onset, offset) intervals. The training split contains 14,148 intervals and the test split 2,558.
Training class counts are 4,312 / 5,048 / 4,788 for classes 0/1/2; test counts are 793 / 900 / 865. Median widths are 116/110/182 samples in training and 114/110/182 in test. The ordering suggests P/QRS/T-like triplets, but the semantic mapping must come from source documentation rather than inference from sequence alone.
The WFDB files are present and link one-to-one to the CSV file_name inside each split. Their headers declare 12 channels, 1,000 samples/s, approximately 9,998–10,000 samples, and a nonstandard unit token mkv. The numerical scale is consistent with microvolt-like values, but the book does not silently relabel mkv as µV without authoritative provenance.

def load_isp(split):
    path = ROOT / "data/isp_delineation_dataset" / f"{split}_isp_delineation_data.csv"
    frame = pd.read_csv(path)
    frame["intervals"] = frame.target.map(ast.literal_eval)
    frame["interval_count"] = frame.intervals.map(len)
    return frame

isp_train = load_isp("train")
isp_test = load_isp("test")

def summarize_isp(frame, split):
    intervals = [x for row in frame.intervals for x in row]
    return {
        "split": split, "records": len(frame), "age_mean": frame.age.mean(),
        "age_sd": frame.age.std(), "sex_0": (frame.sex == 0).sum(),
        "sex_1": (frame.sex == 1).sum(), "intervals": len(intervals),
        "class_0": sum(x[0] == 0 for x in intervals),
        "class_1": sum(x[0] == 1 for x in intervals),
        "class_2": sum(x[0] == 2 for x in intervals),
    }

5.3.3 Interval integrity


Code
def interval_audit(frame, split):
    lengths = isp_headers.loc[
        isp_headers.split == split
    ].set_index("file_name").samples
    rows = []
    for _, record in frame.iterrows():
        xs = record.intervals
        record_length = int(lengths.loc[record.file_name])
        rows.append({
            "file_name": record.file_name,
            "valid_class": all(x[0] in {0, 1, 2} for x in xs),
            "positive_width": all(x[1] < x[2] for x in xs),
            "within_window": all(0 <= x[1] < x[2] <= record_length for x in xs),
            "sorted": all(xs[j][1] <= xs[j + 1][1] for j in range(len(xs) - 1)),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

isp_interval_integrity = pd.concat([
    interval_audit(isp_train, "train").assign(split="train"),
    interval_audit(isp_test, "test").assign(split="test"),
])
display(isp_interval_integrity.groupby("split").agg(
    records=("file_name", "count"),
    invalid_class=("valid_class", lambda x: (~x).sum()),
    invalid_width=("positive_width", lambda x: (~x).sum()),
    outside_window=("within_window", lambda x: (~x).sum()),
    unsorted=("sorted", lambda x: (~x).sum()),
))
invalid_isp = isp_interval_integrity.loc[
    ~(isp_interval_integrity.valid_class & isp_interval_integrity.positive_width & isp_interval_integrity.within_window & isp_interval_integrity.sorted)
]

Those records are quarantined from any benchmark or width summary until the source owner adjudicates whether the intervals should be clipped, corrected, or excluded. The descriptive counts above intentionally inventory the raw files and must not be mistaken for a cleaned training contract. The ranked table makes outlier selection algorithmic. ECG010 and ECG008 appear because of their decoded amplitudes, not because they were selected after viewing model performance. They remain in the primary descriptive analysis; robust medians and leave-one-record-out sensitivity should accompany means.
Fully measured limb leads make Sunnybrook valuable for detecting models that exploit algebraic limb-lead identities while failing on independently acquired morphology.


5.4.3 Hyperfeatures and evidence level
The Philips XLI pipeline supplies global heart rate, PR/QRS/QT/QTc and axes; per-lead P/Q/R/S/T amplitudes; P/QRS/T durations; ST onset/midpoint/J+80/end/slope; measured-lead flags; and diagnostic statements. These are machine-derived reference features, not cardiologist-adjudicated truth.
The set includes sinus rhythms, atrial fibrillation/flutter, old inferior MI, chamber/conduction findings, poor R-wave progression, and a mislaced-lead warning. With only 20 records, these are cases for external stress testing, not stable prevalence or broad clinical-effect estimation.


5.4.4 Retained transients and robust analysis
The comprehensive package retains a 20.44 mV V5 transient in ECG010 and a 6.66 mV V4 transient in ECG008 without clipping. Final analyses should report median/IQR and per-record influence alongside means, with an explicitly labeled sensitivity analysis excluding flagged transients. Silent removal would hide a real robustness failure.
Provenance also notes an approximately 18 µV physical Einthoven residual. This is an empirical acquisition reference, not a universal “errors below 18 µV are perfect” threshold: lead-law residual and reconstruction error are different quantities.
Sunnybrook superclass endpoints use non-adjudicated Philips statement proxies. ECGFounder has probability-fidelity evaluation only because compatible 150-task labels are absent. Those qualifications must appear beside every result table, not only in an appendix.

text:
6.1 Why this chapter appears before model results
This chapter is an input-data audit, not evidence that one reconstruction loss is clinically superior. The local Zhejiang collection can support a useful external morphology benchmark, but the current result table contains only a ground-truth ceiling row. It therefore cannot yet estimate an MSE-versus-MMD contrast. Keeping that distinction visible prevents an available dataset from being mistaken for a completed experiment.
The audit below reads the files in data/zhejiang directly. It establishes what is physically present, checks signal-label pairing and mask integrity, and states the provenance information that is still missing. Later chapters may cite this cohort only within those bounds.
Code
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import pickle

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

REPO = Path("..").resolve()
DATA_ROOT = REPO / "data" / "zhejiang"
ECG_ROOT = DATA_ROOT / "ecg"
LABEL_ROOT = DATA_ROOT / "label"
RESULT_CSV = REPO / "results" / "zhejiang_benchmark" / "zhejiang_delineation_evaluation.csv"

LEADS = ("I", "II", "III", "aVR", "aVL", "aVF", "V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6")

def sha256_file(path, chunk_bytes=1024 * 1024):
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(chunk_bytes), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()

if not ECG_ROOT.is_dir() or not LABEL_ROOT.is_dir():
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        "The Zhejiang audit requires data/zhejiang/ecg and data/zhejiang/label."
    )

6.5 What the current result artifact can—and cannot—say
The table below is loaded rather than hard-coded. A ground-truth ceiling is a pipeline sanity check: applying the reference mask to itself should produce perfect overlap and zero boundary error. It is not a reconstruction-model result and supplies no loss-function comparison.


Code
if RESULT_CSV.exists():
    current_results = pd.read_csv(RESULT_CSV)
    display(current_results)
    ceiling = current_results.loc[current_results["model_id"] == "ground_truth_ceiling"]
    metric_columns = [
        c for c in current_results.columns
        if c != "model_id" and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(current_results[c])
    ]
    overlap_columns = [c for c in metric_columns if "dice" in c.lower() or "f1" in c.lower()]
    error_columns = [c for c in metric_columns if "mae" in c.lower() or "error" in c.lower()]
    ceiling_valid = (
        len(ceiling) == 1
        and all(np.isclose(float(ceiling.iloc[0][c]), 1.0) for c in overlap_columns)
        and all(np.isclose(float(ceiling.iloc[0][c]), 0.0) for c in error_columns)
    )
    model_rows = current_results.loc[current_results["model_id"] != "ground_truth_ceiling"]
    if not ceiling_valid:
        display(Markdown(
            "> [!CAUTION]\n"
            "> **BLOCKED sanity gate.** The row labelled `ground_truth_ceiling` is not a "
            "perfect mask self-comparison. It may instead be a detector-versus-annotation result "
            "or an evaluator defect. No downstream delineation or loss-function claim is admissible "
            "until the row is correctly relabelled or the self-check is repaired."
        ))
    status = pd.DataFrame([
        ("Artifact SHA-256", sha256_file(RESULT_CSV)),
        ("Rows in artifact", str(len(current_results))),
        ("Ground-truth ceiling rows", str((current_results["model_id"] == "ground_truth_ceiling").sum())),
        ("Reconstruction-model rows", str(len(model_rows))),
        ("Ceiling sanity gate", "PASS" if ceiling_valid else "FAIL — downstream claims blocked"),
        ("MSE-versus-MMD contrast estimable", "Yes" if ceiling_valid and len(model_rows) >= 2 else "No"),

6.7 Interpretation boundary
The local files establish a paired 12-lead signal-and-mask corpus with internally consistent array structure. They do not, by themselves, establish cohort independence, diagnostic labels, RVOT/LVOT composition, sampling rate, voltage units, or licensing terms. Those facts require an authoritative README, paper, or data dictionary. Until model rows are generated under the protocol above, this chapter supports dataset readiness work—not a claim that MMD, MSE, or any other objective better preserves clinical morphology.

title: 7  PTB-XL Tensor, Lead, and Preprocessing Contract
text:
7.1 The contract actually used by training
The active reconstruction study reads precomputed PTB-XL tensors from data/ptb_xl/tensors/{train,val,test}. Each file is named by ECG record ID and contains a 12-by-5,000 floating-point array in canonical lead order. The model observes I, II, and V2—indices [0, 1, 7]—and reconstructs the nine remaining leads. Earlier text in this chapter incorrectly selected II, V1, and V5; that would define a different inverse problem and has been removed.
The content-pinned training contract declares 500 Hz, 10 seconds, mV, no normalization, train folds 1–8, validation fold 9, test fold 10, and batch size 1,024 for the running generation. “No normalization” and “no bandpass” mean the tensor values are passed to the model as stored; the Fourier/filter example later in this chapter is exploratory and is not a production transform.
Code
from pathlib import Path
import hashlib
import json

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

title: 7  PTB-XL Tensor, Lead, and Preprocessing Contract
text:
7.2 Canonical lead geometry
The stored order is
[I,II,III,aVR,aVL,aVF,V1,V2,V3,V4,V5,V6].
The limb leads are linear combinations of three electrode potentials:
I=\Phi_{LA}-\Phi_{RA},\qquad II=\Phi_{LL}-\Phi_{RA},\qquad III=II-I,
aVR=-\frac{I+II}{2},\qquad aVL=I-\frac{II}{2},\qquad aVF=II-\frac{I}{2}.
These identities motivate cross-lead residual checks, but digitized clinical leads need not satisfy them to machine precision because of acquisition, filtering, quantization, timing, and export behavior. The precordial leads V1–V6 are separate chest-electrode measurements relative to a central terminal; they cannot be exactly derived from I and II.
The model observes I, II, and V2. The choice combines two limb views with one early precordial view; it is a study design choice, not a claim that this is the optimal sensor placement or that a smartwatch records all three.
crumbs: 7  PTB-XL Tensor, Lead, and Preprocessing Contract

title: 7  PTB-XL Tensor, Lead, and Preprocessing Contract
text:
7.3 Executable dataset loader
The loader below mirrors the active tensor semantics: numeric record ordering, weights_only=True, float conversion, shape validation, no signal normalization, and selection of [0,1,7]. Padding to 5,120 is performed in the U-Net training/evaluation path, not persisted in these tensor files.


Code
class PTBXLTensorDataset(Dataset):
    lead_names = ("I", "II", "III", "aVR", "aVL", "aVF", "V1", "V2", "V3", "V4", "V5", "V6")
    observed_indices = (0, 1, 7)

    def __init__(self, tensor_root, split):
        self.split = split
        self.files = sorted(
            (Path(tensor_root) / split).glob("*.pt"),
            key=lambda path: int(path.stem),
        )
        if not self.files:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"No tensors found for split {split!r}")

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.files)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        path = self.files[index]
        target = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True).float()
        if tuple(target.shape) != (12, 5000):
            raise ValueError(f"Expected [12,5000] at {path}, got {tuple(target.shape)}")
        if not torch.isfinite(target).all():
            raise ValueError(f"Non-finite tensor at {path}")
        observed = target[list(self.observed_indices)]
        return observed, target, int(path.stem)

datasets = {split: PTBXLTensorDataset(TENSOR_ROOT, split) for split in ("train", "val", "test")}

section: 7.5 Spectral audit of the stored signal
text:
7.5 Spectral audit of the stored signal
A periodogram is a record-level diagnostic, not proof of a universal “QRS band.” The example below uses Welch’s method on the named Lead I tensor. Spectral summaries depend on window, detrending, segment length, and any upstream acquisition filtering, so those choices remain visible.


Code
fs = contract["preprocessing"]["sample_rate_hz"]
lead_i = target[0].numpy()
frequencies, power = signal.welch(
    lead_i, fs=fs, window="hann", nperseg=1000, noverlap=500, detrend="constant"
)
fig = go.Figure(go.Scatter(
    x=frequencies, y=10 * np.log10(np.maximum(power, np.finfo(float).tiny)),
    mode="lines", name="Lead I Welch PSD",
))
fig.update_layout(
    title=f"PTB-XL ECG {ecg_id}, Lead I — exploratory spectrum",
    xaxis_title="Frequency (Hz)", yaxis_title="Power/frequency (dB, mV²/Hz)",
    height=420,
)
fig.update_xaxes(range=[0, 100])
fig.show()


                            
                                            
Welch spectrum of the named, unfiltered stored Lead I tensor.

title: 7  PTB-XL Tensor, Lead, and Preprocessing Contract
text:
7.6 Filtering demonstration—not the training transform
Zero-phase forward-backward filtering applies a causal filter in both directions, canceling net phase while squaring its magnitude response. It can still change peak amplitudes, boundary shapes, edge samples, and noise content. The comparison below is therefore a sensitivity illustration only. The content-pinned checkpoints were trained on the unfiltered stored tensors, and filtered signals must not be substituted at inference without a separately trained/evaluated contract.


Code
sos = signal.butter(3, [0.5, 45.0], btype="bandpass", fs=fs, output="sos")
filtered = signal.sosfiltfilt(sos, lead_i)
window = time_seconds < 3

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=time_seconds[window], y=lead_i[window], mode="lines",
    name="Stored Lead I (production tensor)", line=dict(width=1.3),
))
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=time_seconds[window], y=filtered[window], mode="lines",
    name="0.5–45 Hz demonstration", line=dict(width=1.3),
))
fig.update_layout(
    title=f"FILTER DEMONSTRATION — PTB-XL ECG {ecg_id}, not a training transform",
    xaxis_title="Time (s)", yaxis_title="mV", height=420,
)
fig.show()


                            
                                            
Exploratory filtering of one real record; the green trace is not a production model input.

title: 14  Smartwatch Simulator Transfer and Frozen-Classifier Fidelity
text:
14.5 Interpretation boundary
The artifacts show that reconstruction changes a frozen classifier’s probabilities and that change varies across tasks, devices, architectures, and objectives. Before a clinical transfer claim, the study still requires record-level outputs joined to independently adjudicated labels, patient-level identity and clustered uncertainty, prespecified primary tasks and multiplicity control, simple baselines, per-lead waveform endpoints, alignment sensitivity, protocol-stratified failure cases, and a passed independent post-run audit.
Reproduction sources are smartwatch_protocol_metrics.csv, smartwatch_task_fidelity.csv, clinical_database_manifest.json, and FINAL_COMPLETION.json under results/factorial_v4_clinical/. Rendering is read-only and generates no CSV.

import plotly.express as px

def nondominated(group, x, y):
    values = group[[x, y]].to_numpy()
    return np.array([not np.any((values[:,0] >= a) & (values[:,1] >= b) &
                                ((values[:,0] > a) | (values[:,1] > b))) for a,b in values])

valid_master = master.loc[master.inference_status == "valid"].copy()

title: 13  Generation-Bound 48-Cell Factorial Benchmark
text:
13.9 Interpretation boundary
The defensible result is architecture- and endpoint-specific: auxiliary shape/distribution terms can change QRS/ST preservation and waveform fidelity, while frozen-classifier AUROC need not move in the same direction. No cell wins every endpoint, and post hoc maxima are exploratory. Current authority resides in results/factorial_v4/ plus the generation registry and protocol audit; the removed comprehensive_latest_48_models path is not used.

from pathlib import Path

        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1024 * 1024), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()

required = [LABEL_AUDIT, PREFLIGHT, FINAL]

    required += [CLIN / "figures" / f"{stem}.png", CLIN / "figures" / f"{stem}.provenance.json"]

text:
18.8 Interpretation boundary
Engineering integrity is necessary but not sufficient for scientific validity. A healthy database, complete queue, or matching hash cannot prove a clinical claim. Conversely, a scientifically sensible analysis is not releasable when generation identity, missingness, or execution state is ambiguous. This atlas makes those layers visible and treats unavailable optional artifacts as unavailable—not as zero, pass, or silently cached evidence.

title: 4  Real-Cohort EDA, Integrity Checks, and Deep Diagnostics
text:
4.5 Per-dataset waveform UMAP atlas
The repository reference manual at external/dataset_info.md enumerates seven clinical signal cohorts plus wearable/noise stress streams. This executable atlas reconciles that document with the files physically available at render time. It includes PTB-XL, EchoNext, LUDB, ISP, Sunnybrook, Zhejiang, and RDB. NSTDB/Fitbit stress streams are not plotted as an eighth clinical-cohort UMAP: they are perturbation sources, and no independently versioned raw stress corpus is present beneath the checkout’s data/ entry. Treating generated SNR variants as independent patients would inflate the apparent sample size.
Some statements in the reference manual are stronger than the locally verifiable evidence. In particular, the current data/rdb/ entry is empty, so RDB is read from the generation-bound waveform/delineation cache; ISP provenance and class semantics remain unresolved by the files themselves; and Zhejiang’s geographic/demographic description is not encoded in its arrays. The plots use those datasets, but their legends and interpretations remain inside the local evidence boundary.

4.5.1 Shared feature and sampling contract
Each ECG is mapped to the same 96-dimensional vector: for every canonical lead, RMS amplitude, interquartile range, 1st-to-99th percentile range, derivative RMS, and four relative Fourier-energy quartiles. Features are robust-scaled within each dataset. This representation is deliberately transparent and is not a learned ECG-AIM latent representation. Because sampling rates and units differ—and Zhejiang’s units/rate are not independently documented in its local tree—no pooled cross-dataset UMAP is used to claim domain similarity.
Sampling is deterministic and bounded. Small cohorts use all available records; larger cohorts use a SHA-256-ranked sample that is invariant to directory order. Raw signals are reduced one record at a time and are never copied into the HTML. RDB acquisition identifiers are replaced with one-way, namespace-scoped display tokens before plotting.

The diagnostics are part of the result, not decoration. Trustworthiness at k=5 measures whether local neighborhoods in the robust-scaled feature space survive projection. The stability column compares all pairwise distances from the seed-42 map with seeds 7 and 101 using Spearman rank correlation; it is rotation/reflection invariant. Low values invalidate visual cluster claims.
Panel B in every curated figure is the main protection against an attractive but misleading projection. It compares same-group nearest-neighbor frequency in the original 96-dimensional space, in the two-dimensional UMAP, and under the observed group imbalance. If the UMAP bar rises far above the original-space bar, the projection has visually amplified grouping. Panel C returns to a raw, purpose-linked measurement rather than asking UMAP to carry the claim.


4.5.2 PTB-XL — development-cohort support and split transport
PTB-XL is the reconstruction development cohort: 21,799 ten-second, 12-lead records in paired 500 Hz and 100 Hz releases. Official folds define training (1–8), validation (9), and holdout test (10); the patient-overlap audit above is the relevant independence gate. Diagnostic SCP labels and clinical metadata support reconstruction, morphology, and downstream diagnostic-retention work.
The curated question is not whether diagnoses form attractive clusters. It is whether official splits occupy comparable broad waveform support. Panel C shows global RMS by split; a split-specific island plus shifted RMS would trigger a device/site/quality investigation before interpreting model generalization.

4.5.3 EchoNext — structural-heart-disease phenotype
EchoNext contains 100,000 ECG–echocardiogram pairs, but only the 5,442-record official test waveform array is locally retained. Signals are 250 Hz and stored after released clipping and train-set normalization; the earlier audit reverses that affine transform for physical interpretation. Twelve echo-derived endpoints make this a transport and downstream-task cohort, not extra PTB-XL reconstruction training data.
The figure asks whether the released composite SHD endpoint aligns with broad ECG phenotype while showing LVEF outside the embedding. Visible separation is hypothesis generating: spectrum, care setting, age, and endpoint co-occurrence remain potential explanations.

4.5.4 LUDB — expert morphology and atrial-fibrillation contrast
LUDB contributes 200 ten-second, 500 Hz, 12-lead ECGs with independently cardiologist-annotated P, QRS, and T boundaries on every lead. It is a morphology/delineation benchmark. Header diagnoses overlap and are not one mutually exclusive disease target.
AF is used as a narrow contrast because organized P-wave behavior is relevant to delineation. The 15 AF records are compared with the heterogeneous remainder, and age is shown explicitly as a basic confounding axis. This is not an estimate of AF diagnostic performance.

4.5.5 ISP — delineation split-shift audit under unresolved provenance
The local ISP package contains 403 training and 72 test records linked to 12-channel WFDB signals and serialized interval targets. Headers declare 1,000 Hz and the nonstandard unit token mkv. Although the reference manual assigns P/QRS/T semantics and a multicenter origin, no citation, license, source ID, or authoritative class dictionary is present locally. Those claims remain provisional here.
The defensible question is whether the provided test split shifts relative to training in waveform features or interval burden. Patient independence remains unverified, so split mixing cannot certify leakage freedom.

4.5.6 Sunnybrook — physical-acquisition quality control
Sunnybrook is a 20-record local Philips XML transfer set with owner metadata and 179 machine-extracted features. The production decoder verifies sampling rate, lead order, resolution, and the centered ten-second crop. Cohort selection, subject multiplicity, adjudication, distribution authority, and the stronger “fully measured gold standard” claim are not independently established locally.
With 20 records, a disease-cluster UMAP would be especially unstable. This figure marks the two records whose maximum absolute amplitude exceeds 5 mV and shows the raw maxima. Its purpose is retained-transient and influence analysis, not prevalence generalization.

4.5.7 Zhejiang — dense-mask burden and waveform phenotype
The Zhejiang tree contains 334 record-level masks and 4,008 lead files (12 per record), each 20,000 samples long. Local arrays establish signal–mask pairing and the observed 0/1/2/3 mask convention. They do not independently establish institution, ethnicity, units, sampling rate, patient independence, or clinical diagnoses; those fields require external provenance.
The embedding is colored by QRS-mask-coverage quartile and Panel C exposes the underlying percentage. This tests whether gross segmentation burden tracks waveform phenotype; it does not turn a derived quartile into a clinical class.

4.5.8 RDB — rhythm-diverse delineation and P-wave absence
RDB supplies 2,399 ten-second, 500 Hz, 12-lead records spanning eight canonical rhythm groups with lead-specific and consensus P/QRS/T intervals. The raw data/rdb/ entry is empty in this checkout, so this figure reads the generation-bound cache built from the raw CSV/annotation package. Cache records are source-bound, while public display labels are pseudonymized.
The figure asks whether rhythm diversity corresponds to broad waveform regimes and shows P-mask coverage by rhythm. This is directly relevant to AF hallucination: a model should not invent organized P waves when the reference mask supports their absence. Rhythm separation itself is not reconstruction quality.

4.5.10 Cross-figure interpretation and falsification rules
For each panel, the only admissible first-pass question is whether its displayed group is locally mixed or separated in this specified feature representation. Separation does not prove diagnosis, site, physiology, or model learnability. PTB-XL and ISP colors are split diagnostics; EchoNext and RDB use released labels; LUDB uses a header-text AF indicator; Sunnybrook and Zhejiang colors are explicitly derived QC strata rather than clinical ground truth.
A visual finding is worth following only when trustworthiness and seed stability are adequate. The next test must operate in the original 96-dimensional feature space—for example, patient-grouped classification or a prespecified two-sample test with multiplicity control. Repeating UMAP until an attractive separation appears is not a valid analysis.
